title: Section rehearsals and Redman's rule to follow the first man
summary: Calloway was not a technical musician, so the sidemen rehearsed sections themselves; Jackson recalls Redman's advice to phrase with the lead player.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: But, now, let's see, to get that band -- the one thing about that band, you tell me about it, you guys were so conscientious because Cab, not being what we call really a musician, he was a great entertainer and he always got good musicians because he was paying good money and he wanted to surround himself with good musicians, but he didn't really know how to rehearse a band. And I remember we used to all get together and have section rehearsal and you guys used to get it together and then when we got on the stage, --
Well, I'll tell you, do you remember,
too, that a lot of times if a guy made an arrangement, whoever made the arrangement, sometime Calloway would have him just run it over.
Then we would take it from there, --
But the section rehearsal was the thing that really made you have a lot of precision, --

-- and you could feel each other. And I have to go back to Don Redman, too, that taught me how to play with a section. Don Redman used to say all the time, 'Listen to the first man and you cannot go wrong. If you listen to the way he phrases something and you phrase it with him, you will have a section,' --
-- you see. You know, today there's so much individualism till the kids, I don't know, they just don't learn this.
